# Sleep vs Lock vs Shutdown vs Restart

Here's what each one means for your computer:

## **Sleep** 🏛️
- Saves your work to RAM (random access memory) 
- Uses minimal power but keeps the system responsive when you wake it
- Fast wake time (a few seconds)
- Your apps stay open and in their last state
- Not recommended if leaving for long periods or if you think you'll forget to lock

## **Lock** 🔒
- Only protects your session from others who might use your PC
- Your computer still runs on full power
- Apps continue in background
- You don't need to log in again after unlocking, but other users won't be able to access files you created

## **Shutdown** 🛌
- Completely turns off the computer - all power goes out
- Takes longer to boot back up (usually 1-5 minutes depending on system)
- Saves RAM and battery life for long periods
- All apps close completely
- You must log in again after restarting

## **Restart** 🔁
- Similar to shutdown but turns off and back on as part of the same process
- Often used to fix issues or update software
- Usually cleaner and more reliable than forcing a shutdown
- Your files will stay intact (unlike when you accidentally force shut down)

| Action | Power Use | Best For |
|--------|-----------|----------|
| Sleep | Low | Short breaks |
| Lock | Medium | Security while away briefly |
| Shutdown | None | Going home for a long time |
| Restart | Temporary high then low | Fixes problems, updates |
